verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents an official MCP server, CLI, and API tokens for flag creation/toggling (docs-10,11,12,37,40), plus a dedicated Approvals workflow and change-history/roles system that can require review before changes go live (docs-6,7,36). However, no evidence explicitly confirms that MCP- or CLI-driven agent changes are routed through the approval gate rather than bypassing it, so the integration between agent-facing interfaces and approval enforcement is unconfirmed. Missing for 10: explicit documentation or hands-on proof that MCP/CLI/API writes are forced through approvals rather than applied directly, and independent corroboration of this workflow in practice.
